full_judgment:
2. The petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 116 of 1982 in the Court of District Judge, Rajshahi praying for granting probate of the will alleged to have been executed by their father Kailash Chandra Mondal in their favour on 30-3-1947. Kailash Chandra Mondal died on 2-2-1967. The alleged will was said to be the last will and testament of their father and the petitioners were named as executors in the will. The petitioners further alleged that their father had left behind another son, namely, the respondent and a daughter Renu Bala and the value of the assets under the will was about Taka 80,000.00. They did not make any other petition for probate of the will or for letter of administration of the said properties. 

 3. The respondent filed a written objection denying the petitioners' case and asserting that the alleged will was forged and false, that the value of the property mentioned in the will was not less than Taka 7,00,000, that after the death of their father the properties excluding the properties given to him by his father were amicably partitioned amongst the brothers in a salish and an unregistered partition deed was executed, that accordingly RS record of the property was made in his name, that the alleged will was subsequently created in collusion with one Mofizuddin Chowdhury who was a habitual litigant long after the death of Kailash Chandra Mondal, that the petitioners never asserted about the alleged will when the properties were partitioned, that the respondent was residing in his paternal house, although in a separate mess, and that his father gave him some property separately because of his bad relationship with his step-mother. 

 4. The Miscellaneous Case was ultimately transferred to the Court of the Additional District Judge, Naogaon and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 7 of 1984. The petitioners examined only two witnesses including petitioner No. 1 and the respondent examined four witnesses including himself. 

 5. The learned Additional District Judge upon a consideration of the evidence including the alleged will, Exhibit 1 and the partition deed, Exhibit (Ka) came to the finding that the petitioners failed to prove due execution and attestation of the alleged will, that only one attesting witness was examined although the law required that at least two attesting witnesses should be examined, that the writing in the will appeared to be of recent origin although the paper used appeared to be old, that there was no explanation for the unreasonably long delay of 15 years in filing the application for probate since the death of Kailash Mondal and that the deed of partition as claimed by the respondent was a genuine one. The case was accordingly dismissed by judgment and order dated 19-2-1986. 

 9. It has been noticed that the petitioners' own witness PW 1 admitted in cross-examination that one Mofizuddin Chowdhury who was an attesting witness in the alleged will and had died during the pendency of the proceeding, had set up the petitioners to file the case. Admittedly, except PW 1 no one was examined among the 8 attesting witnesses to prove attestation of the alleged will and no explanation was given for their non-examination even though the law required that at least two attesting witnesses each of whom saw the testator sign or affix his mark should be examined by the propounded of the will. The long delay of 15 years in filing the application for probate was not explained. The alleged will was found not to be physically genuine. There is thus no scope at all for any interference.
